prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The SNP’s 1997 manifesto argues Scotland is wealthy, subsidises the UK, and can “pay its way” as an independent state. Independence is framed as the route to better public services, full employment, social justice and modern governance. The party commits to a written constitution and Bill of Rights; a unicameral parliament elected by proportional representation; entrenched local government (also PR-elected); reform of the monarchy; and citizenship based on residency or birth. It asserts automatic EU membership, open borders with England, protected pensions/investments, and an equal social union with neighbours.

Path to independence: a majority of SNP MPs would trigger negotiations with the UK and EU, followed by a referendum on the independence settlement within 6–12 months and a fresh election.

Economy and taxation: Target full employment and 100,000 additional jobs via enterprise support, skills, R&D, exports, tourism and infrastructure. Cut corporation tax (main to 30%, small to 18%), abolish Class IV NICs, introduce banded business rates, and limit the rate multiplier. Adopt the EU Social Chapter, a negotiated minimum wage (half median male earnings), and a Charter for Trade Union Rights. Personal tax: introduce a 15p starter rate, widen the basic-rate band, remove the NI ceiling for high earners, and cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5%.

Social justice and health: Increase child benefit and restore benefits to 16–17s. Pension package: weekly rises (£3 single/£5 couples), a Cold Climate Allowance, remove utility standing charges for pensioners, and end means‑testing for residential care. Rebuild a “real” NHS by scrapping the internal market, integrating planning through national/local health commissions, adding £35m a year, reintegrating dentistry, reforming prescription charges, banning tobacco advertising and raising tobacco duty. Establish a Scottish Food and Consumer Health Agency. Tackle crime with “zero tolerance” on community offences, more resources for police and prosecutors, effective alternatives to prison, and a total ban on handguns.

Education and housing: Hire 700 teachers, repair schools, guarantee internet access, provide free nursery for 3–4s, restore student grants, expand training and apprenticeships. Support Gaelic/Scots and minority faith studies. Address the housing crisis by transferring 75% of council housing debt to central government, building up to 20,000 affordable homes in four years, upgrading substandard/damp homes, strengthening homelessness duties, protecting new/improved stock from discounted right-to-buy, and creating a new accountable housing agency.

Rural, environment, energy, transport: Abolish feudal tenure, create a Land Commission and all‑Scotland land register, devolve foreshore powers. Reform CAP, diversify agriculture, restore beef markets via traceability, strengthen fisheries management and processing, double woodland cover, and bolster crofting. Empower SEPA, set national environmental targets, end nuclear reprocessing at Dounreay (pivot to decommissioning and renewables), phase out nuclear power, and leverage Scotland’s oil and gas (equidistance share) while correcting discriminatory gas pricing. Modernise rail (publicly owned Railtrack Scotland), integrate buses, remove bridge tolls (including Skye), improve ferries, and adjust Air Passenger Duty for remote areas. Expand telecoms competition and rural connectivity; promote internet adoption.

Europe, world, defence: Full EU membership with voting power and increased MEPs; targeted, trade‑focused diplomacy; membership of UN, Council of Europe, Commonwealth; a British Isles association. Create professional Scottish Defence Forces, withdraw Trident, negotiate phased NATO exit while cooperating via EU/WEU/OSCE/PfP, and establish a peacekeeping college; promote defence diversification.

Finances: A fully costed four‑year budget funds enterprise, social, education and aid priorities from Scotland’s relative fiscal surplus, growth, defence savings and lower debt interest—while repaying £6.6bn of national debt over four years.
